reuse.why: Replaces the scattered getDateWithSkippedWeekend ternaries with shared applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay, isNonWorkingDay and skipsWeekendOccurrences, and every consumer (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, schedule-template) uses them.

duplication.why: The daily-skip dispatch (skipsWeekendOccurrences, then filter by isNonWorkingDay, else applyWeekendRule) is rewritten at four call sites, and the `7 + holidays.length` look-ahead heuristic appears in both getNextDate and getUpcomingDates.

placement.why: Rule helpers live in shared/schedules.ts where the tree keeps schedule date logic; the new handler sits beside getUpcomingDates.

scope.why: Changes follow the five steps; rule-utils gains frequency/holidays in the schedule data, which the shared predicate needs.

maintainability.why: Helpers are clear, but the shared definition covers only the move, so a change to the daily-skip rule or the look-ahead still has to be made at four sites with differently shaped code.

bypasses_abstraction.where: schedule-template.ts createScheduleList (own `skipsWeekendDays ? baseDate : applyWeekendRuleToDay(...)` plus its own isNonWorkingDay check) and getNextDate (`!noSkipWeekend && !skipsWeekendDays` guard around applyWeekendRule) decide part of the rule locally.

disguised_duplication.where: The same skip-or-move dispatch is reshaped per site: pickDate in getNextDate, a .filter in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange, and resolveDate plus a guarded accumulation in schedule-template.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay/getDateWithSkippedWeekend gain a holidays parameter; the daily-schedule exception is never put inside the shared rule, so getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and createScheduleList each re-implement it around the helper.
